# Ruby Gillis

## Overview

- **Age:** Early twenties (around 20-21 years old at the end of Volume 3)
- **Gender:** Female
- **Status:** Deceased
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, Canada
- **Role:** Schoolteacher

## Appearance

Ruby was considered one of the prettiest girls in Avonlea, renowned for her brilliant fair complexion, large blue eyes, and long, gleaming golden hair. As she grew into womanhood, her beauty matured into an ethereal, delicate quality. Towards the end of her life, her cheeks carried a bright, feverish flush that heightened her radiant appearance.

## Personality

Ruby was sentimentally romantic, lightheaded, and endlessly preoccupied with beaux and suitors. Though somewhat shallow and prone to gushing emotional displays, she was sweet-tempered and held genuine affection for her childhood friends. As her illness progressed, she harbored a deep, quiet terror of death, clinging desperately to the simple pleasures of the world she loved.

## Traits

- Vain and romantic
- Giddy and sentimental
- Terrified of dying and leaving youth behind
- Sweet-natured

## Abilities

- Attracting numerous male suitors
- Teaching school
- Fancy needlework and embroidery

## Goals

- To be courted by many young men and have a traditional romantic life
- To recover her health and continue living

## History

Ruby grew up in Avonlea as one of Anne Shirley's primary classmates and joined the Story Club in her girlhood. She later attended Queen's Academy with Anne and their peers, successfully obtaining a teacher's certificate before taking up a teaching position outside Avonlea. Throughout her adolescence and early adulthood, Ruby was famous for having more 'beaux' than any other girl in her circle, constantly talking of romance and marriage. However, her life was cut short when she contracted galloping consumption (tuberculosis). Returning home to Avonlea, she spent her final summer sitting in her family's garden, trying to ignore the gravity of her illness. Shortly before her passing, she shared a poignant heart-to-heart conversation with Anne, confessing her fear of heaven because it lacked the familiar romance and frivolity she cherished. She passed away peacefully during the night at the end of the summer.

## Background by volume

- Grew up as part of the large Gillis family in Avonlea
- Attended Avonlea School alongside Anne Shirley and Diana Barry
- Studied at Queen's Academy to earn her teaching license

## Affiliations

- The Avonlea Story Club — Member
- Avonlea Young People's Improvement Society (AYPIS) — Member
